scope: Bounded per-segment allocation/free accounting and isolated runtime integration
instrumentation: Each Block allocation receives an ID; Block Drop records its release. Relaxed counters assert every allocated ID is released exactly once after the model closure destroys all handles. No extra Acquire/Release publication. Observation budget: 128 segments; preemption bound 2, max branches 10000.
commands: Generate --lap 4 or --lap 32; retired adds --omit-retired-free, final adds --omit-final-free. Prepare cargo generate-lockfile --offline; run cargo test --manifest-path <directory>/Cargo.toml --offline --locked --lib. Negative controls filter slots::drop_once_across_retirement_and_abandoned_tail -- --exact. DEV/TEST DEBUG=0, CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0.
negative_diagnostic: segment allocation 0 (retired) or 1 (final) was not released
environment: Initial runs exhausted disk. Only final logs with test summaries and expected assertions are credited. Generated build directories were removed; sources, adaptation diffs, provenance, lockfiles and logs retained.

isolated_integration.selection: HEAD plus WorkQueue/WorkStealer change and three SegQueue probe files; PendingWork block excluded using a separate temporary index. Original index and worktree preserved.
isolated_integration.command: CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/dev/Work/bml/target/segmented-isolated-build cargo test -p bml-runtime --all-features --locked

limits: Leak controls establish sensitivity to omitted releases, not arbitrary premature reclamation. Raw block pointers remain native; counter success is not a general use-after-free or liveness proof. Isolated runtime tests are not a complete workspace gate.
remaining: Review protection against premature reclamation and finish the isolated integration gate/commit before closing 9.2.
